bottom_line: Early rhythm control vs usual care reduced the first primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.79; 96% confidence interval, 0.66 to 0.94).
implications: In patients with early atrial fibrillation and cardiovascular conditions, the strategy of early rhythm control was associated with fewer first-primary-outcome events than usual care (3.9 vs 5.0 per 100 person-years; hazard ratio, 0.79; 96% confidence interval, 0.66 to 0.94). The mean number of nights spent in the hospital did not differ significantly between groups (5.8±21.9 vs 5.1±15.5 days per year; P = 0.23). The primary composite safety outcome occurred in similar proportions (16.6% vs 16.0), while serious adverse events of special interest related to rhythm-control therapy were more frequent with early rhythm control (4.9% vs 1.4%).
